The ColecoVision has no back buffer (1K of RAM), so showGameScreen()
repaints the table straight to VRAM. Every server poll would otherwise
redraw the whole table even when nothing changed -- invisible on a real
display (identical bytes rewritten in place) but a waste, and it makes a
redraw always be in flight, which tears on capture. Skip the repaint
when the fetched state is byte-for-byte what is already on screen.
state is the reply window here (see src/misc.h), valid until the next
fuji_* call -- which is exactly now, right after the fetch. A one-word
sum is enough: a rare collision just defers a repaint to the next
differing poll. requestPlayerMove() still runs, so our own turn (where
the countdown does change the state every second) always draws.
The NES draws through cc65's vblank ring buffer, a few dozen tiles a
frame, so an unchanged repaint there costs a backlog the next real
change has to queue behind. Its state is an ordinary object in WRAM.
So is the Master System's; its VDP takes a table's worth of writes
easily, but there is no point shipping an unchanged one every poll.
The H89's H19 terminal is on a 9600 baud line. Its renderer sends only
the cells that differ, so an unchanged repaint costs no bytes, but it
still re-sweeps the active player's highlight; skip it.

H19 terminal screen for the H89 port.
The screen is drawn by cell codes, one byte each: bit 7 is reverse video and
the low seven bits are the H19's own character ROM index (444-29) --
0x00-0x1F the graphics characters, 0x7F the graphics bullet, 0x20-0x7E
ASCII -- the same form the terminal keeps its screen in.
Drawing goes into a back buffer; flush() sends the terminal only the cells
that differ from what it already shows, with as few cursor-address (ESC Y),
reverse-video (ESC p/q) and graphics-mode (ESC F/G) changes as it can, and
erases (ESC K, ESC E) where they are cheaper than spaces. The console runs at
9600 baud, and the shared game code repaints the whole table every poll.
Row 24 is the H19's 25th line, which termInit() turns on for the status bar.
